title: Opposition and Completion
overview: Nehemiah Chapter 6 details the final opposition faced by Nehemiah and the Jewish people as they complete the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall. Despite persistent threats, deception, and attempts to intimidate him, Nehemiah remains steadfast, relying on God’s strength to finish the work. The chapter highlights the spiritual warfare behind physical opposition and demonstrates the power of faith and perseverance. The completion of the wall in just fifty-two days marks a significant moment of divine favor and national restoration, affirming God’s providence amidst adversity. This chapter serves as a powerful example of leadership, vigilance, and trust in God’s protection during times of conflict.
structure:
**Verses 1-9: Persistent Enemy Tactics.** This section reveals the repeated attempts by Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem to lure Nehemiah into a trap or spread false accusations to halt the rebuilding effort. Nehemiah’s refusal to be distracted underscores his commitment and reliance on God’s strength.

**Verses 10-14: The False Prophecy and Spiritual Deception.** Nehemiah encounters a deceptive prophecy from Shemaiah, who tries to frighten him into hiding in the temple. Nehemiah discerns the plot, recognizing the spiritual warfare and the enemies’ use of false prophecy to undermine him.

**Verses 15-16: The Wall’s Completion and Enemy Discouragement.** The wall is finished in a remarkable fifty-two days, causing the enemies and surrounding peoples to lose heart, acknowledging that the work was accomplished by God’s hand.

**Verses 17-19: Internal Compromise and Correspondence.** The chapter closes with the troubling revelation that some nobles of Judah maintained correspondence with Tobiah, revealing internal divisions and the subtle influence of the enemy within the community.

keyVerses.text: And I sent messengers unto them, saying, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you?
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights Nehemiah’s unwavering focus on God’s work despite external pressures. It teaches the importance of perseverance and prioritizing God’s calling over distractions or threats.

keyVerses.text: For they all made us afraid, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from the work, that it be not done. Now therefore, O God, strengthen my hands.
keyVerses.significance: Nehemiah’s prayer for strength amidst fear exemplifies reliance on God in spiritual and physical battles. It underscores the reality of fear but also the necessity of divine empowerment to overcome opposition.

keyVerses.text: So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days.
keyVerses.significance: The rapid completion of the wall demonstrates God’s blessing on faithful labor. It signifies restoration and protection for Jerusalem, affirming that God honors perseverance and obedience.

keyVerses.text: And it came to pass, that when all our enemies heard thereof, and all the heathen that were about us saw these things, they were much cast down in their own eyes: for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals that the enemies recognized God’s hand in the work, leading to their discouragement. It affirms the theological truth that God’s providence is evident in the success of His people.

characters.name: Nehemiah
characters.description: The governor and leader of the Jewish people who oversees the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall. He demonstrates steadfast faith, discernment, and prayerful dependence on God in the face of opposition.

characters.name: Sanballat
characters.description: An adversary of Nehemiah, likely a Samaritan official, who repeatedly attempts to deceive and intimidate Nehemiah to stop the rebuilding project.

characters.name: Tobiah
characters.description: An Ammonite official allied with Sanballat who opposes the wall’s reconstruction and uses both external threats and internal alliances to undermine Nehemiah.

characters.name: Shemaiah
characters.description: A false prophet hired by Nehemiah’s enemies to frighten him into hiding in the temple, thereby discrediting him and halting the work.

characters.name: God
characters.description: Though not speaking directly, God’s providential protection and strength are central to Nehemiah’s success and the completion of the wall.

themes.description: Nehemiah’s refusal to be distracted or intimidated by repeated enemy tactics illustrates the biblical call to steadfastness in God’s work despite trials.
The chapter reveals that opposition to God’s work includes not only physical threats but also spiritual deception, such as false prophecy and intimidation.
The successful completion of the wall in a short time and the discouragement of enemies highlight God’s active role in protecting and blessing His people.
Nehemiah’s ability to discern falsehood and remain focused exemplifies godly leadership rooted in prayer and wisdom.
The correspondence between Judah’s nobles and Tobiah reveals the danger of internal compromise and the need for faithfulness within the community.

historicalContext: Nehemiah 6 is set in the mid-5th century BC during the Persian period when the Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem to rebuild the city walls after the Babylonian captivity. The city lay in ruins, vulnerable to hostile neighbors including Samaritans and Ammonites, represented here by Sanballat and Tobiah. The plain of Ono, mentioned as a meeting place, was a fertile area west of Jerusalem, often a site of conflict. The political situation was tense, with local officials and neighboring peoples resisting the restoration of Jewish autonomy and security. The rebuilding of the wall was not only a physical restoration but also a spiritual and national renewal under Persian authorization but local opposition.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This perspective emphasizes God’s sovereign providence in sustaining His people through opposition. Nehemiah’s prayer for strength and discernment is seen as a model of dependence on God’s grace in spiritual warfare.

Dispensationalists highlight the historical fulfillment of God’s promises to Israel in the restoration of Jerusalem’s walls as a precursor to future prophetic fulfillments. The opposition reflects ongoing spiritual conflict between God’s kingdom and worldly powers.

Early church interpreters often saw Nehemiah as a type of Christ-like leader who rebuilds the spiritual walls of the church. The enemies represent the devil’s attempts to disrupt God’s redemptive work.

crossReferences.connection: Like Nehemiah’s reliance on God to strengthen his hands, this psalm reminds believers that unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labor in vain.
Paul’s teaching on God’s strength made perfect in weakness parallels Nehemiah’s prayer for God to strengthen his hands amid fear and opposition.
The spiritual warfare behind Nehemiah’s physical opposition echoes Paul’s declaration that our struggle is against spiritual forces of evil.
Nehemiah’s courage and refusal to flee align with God’s command to be strong and courageous, trusting in His presence.
God’s promise to uphold and strengthen His people in times of fear is reflected in Nehemiah’s prayer and confidence.

application: Remain steadfast in God’s work despite opposition or distractions, trusting His strength to complete the task.
Pray for discernment to recognize and resist spiritual deception and false counsel.
Recognize that opposition to godly work often involves both physical and spiritual battles.
Avoid internal compromise by maintaining faithfulness and integrity within the Christian community.
Celebrate and give thanks for God’s providential protection and blessings in accomplishing His purposes.
Lead with courage and wisdom, relying on God’s guidance rather than fear or intimidation.
conclusion: Nehemiah Chapter 6 powerfully illustrates the reality of opposition in God’s work and the necessity of perseverance, prayer, and discernment. Through Nehemiah’s example, believers learn that spiritual warfare is real and that God’s providence enables His people to overcome. The chapter’s culmination in the wall’s completion serves as a testimony to God’s faithfulness and the importance of steadfast leadership. For Christians today, it encourages trust in God’s strength amid trials and calls for vigilance against both external and internal threats to faithfulness.
timeline: c. 445 BC - Rebuilding of Jerusalem’s Wall under Nehemiah’s leadership during the Persian Empire

definitions.definition: A gap or broken place in a wall or fortification, symbolizing vulnerability and incompleteness.
A message claimed to be communicated by God through a prophet, often concerning future events or divine will.
A term used in the Bible to describe people who do not worship the God of Israel, often referring to Gentiles or pagans.
The twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar, corresponding roughly to August-September, significant here as the time of the wall’s completion.
A biblical expression meaning to give courage, power, and endurance to continue a difficult task.

outline.heading: Enemy Attempts to Distract Nehemiah
outline.description: Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem repeatedly invite Nehemiah to meetings, intending harm or distraction, but Nehemiah refuses to abandon the work.

outline.heading: False Accusations and Nehemiah’s Response
outline.description: An open letter falsely accuses Nehemiah of rebellion and ambition, but he denies these claims and prays for God’s strength to continue.

outline.heading: Deception Through False Prophecy
outline.description: Shemaiah, hired by enemies, tries to frighten Nehemiah into hiding in the temple, but Nehemiah discerns the plot and refuses to sin.

outline.heading: Completion of the Wall and Enemy Discouragement
outline.description: The wall is finished in fifty-two days, causing enemies to lose heart as they recognize God’s hand in the work.

outline.heading: Internal Correspondence and Compromise
outline.description: Some nobles of Judah maintain correspondence with Tobiah, revealing internal divisions and the subtle influence of opposition within the community.
